name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread about 153bp, above the 150bp Alert line; Fitch moved France's outlook to negative on 3 Nov
state: France's 10-year yield was 4.79% on 6 Nov against 3.25% on the German Bund, a spread of about 153bp, just above the 150bp Alert line (Trading Economics). Fitch revised France's outlook to negative on 3 Nov, citing public finances, and the 2027 budget faces a 17 Nov deadline (Trading Economics; FXStreet). No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed through to European bank funding and mortgage rates. Holders of French government debt are most exposed to further spread moves.

sources.title: Trading Economics — France 10-year government bond yield
FXStreet — France tests the euro's nerve: what the OAT spread is telling FX traders

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
